Dear Diary, Friday.
Robotics club, week 3. Our line-following robot kept crashing into the wall. Last year I'd have built the whole robot first and tested at the end. This time Nazia and I tried something new: tiny versions.
Monday: just the sensor on a breadboard. Test. It couldn't see black tape under the tube lights. Fixed by adding a shade.
Wednesday: sensor plus one wheel. Test. Wheel turned the wrong way. Swapped two wires.
Today: whole thing, only 30 cm of track. Test. Wobbly on curves. Changed one number in the code.
Each failure took ten minutes to fix, not ten days. I feel weirdly calm. 😌
Aditi

passage: Disha, twenty-one, was studying agricultural engineering and spent her summer in her home village near Bikaner, trying to build a drip-irrigation line for her aunt Sunaina's vegetable patch. Instead of laying pipe across the whole field, she began with one row of tomatoes. Day one: water came out too fast and flooded the roots. She pinched the holes smaller. Day three: the far end got no water. She raised the tank a little on bricks. Day five: a goat chewed a pipe. She added a thorny fence. Each small test showed one problem. By the second week she extended the line to six rows, and Sunaina said the tomatoes had never looked so good.

passage: Ulla's class brief in Aarhus was a board game about city buses, and the final version had to be printed on thick card by Friday. On Monday she didn't touch the card. She drew the board on the back of a pizza box, cut tokens from a cereal carton, and played it with her flatmate Camila after dinner. Camila won in four minutes by blocking every route. Ulla wrote "blocking too strong" on a sticky note and added a rule. Tuesday: they played again, and now nobody could win at all. Note: "too many detours." Wednesday, version three: a game lasted twenty minutes, and Camila demanded a rematch. Thursday, version five: the only complaint was one confusing card, which Ulla reworded. She printed on Friday morning, once, and it worked.
